requirements.statement: The page indicates its default language with the lang and/or xml:lang attribute, either on the html element or on every text element or one of its parents.

citations.quote: Pour chaque page web, l’indication de langue par défaut vérifie-t-elle une de ces conditions
Indication de la langue de traitement principale du document qui peut être présente sur l’élément racine html ou sur chaque élément de la page concerné via les attributs lang et/ou xml:lang

routes.statement: The html element carries the language indication, with the attribute or attributes the document type calls for: lang for HTML up to 4.01 and HTML5, lang and xml:lang for XHTML 1.0 served as text/html, xml:lang for XHTML 1.0 served as application/xhtml+xml and for XHTML 1.1.

citations.quote: L’indication de la langue de la page (attribut `lang` et/ou `xml:lang`) est donnée pour l’élément `html`
Soit au moyen de l’attribut lang sur la balise html si le code est du HTML5 ou du HTML4 ;
Soit au moyen des attributs lang et xml:lang sur la balise html si le code est du XHTML 1.0 ;
Pour XHTML 1.0 servi en "application/xhtml+xml" : attribut xml:lang obligatoire, attribut lang recommandé ;
Pour XHTML 1.1 : attribut xml:lang obligatoire, attribut lang non supporté ;

routes.statement: Every text element carries the language indication itself or through one of its parent elements.

citations.quote: L’indication de la langue de la page (attribut `lang` et/ou `xml:lang`) est donnée sur chaque élément de texte ou sur l’un des éléments parents.
Sinon, vérifier la présence d’une indication de langue sur chaque élément de texte ou l’un de ses parents.

rationale.text: The test has one requirement with two routes: the indication on the html element, or on every text element or a parent of it. The methodology and glossary say which attribute each document type needs (lang for HTML, both for XHTML 1.0 served as text/html, xml:lang for XHTML 1.1 and XHTML served as XML); the document type is known from the doctype and the served content type. Whether the html element carries an attribute is a fact of the DOM. Which texts count as a text element is not: the wording says each text element and does not say whether a field's value, text generated by CSS, an alternative text, the page title or the text of a framed document is one. So the custom check never answers no_fault through the second route. An earlier version did, after checking a list of text items, and a page with an untagged field value outside that list would have passed. The check now decides three cases and abstains on the rest. It answers no_fault when the html element carries the attributes its document type calls for, with a non-empty value; it abstains instead when a rendered frame holds text and its document lacks the indication, because the wording does not say whether a framed document is part of the page here. It faults a page whose html element has neither lang nor xml:lang in any form while some rendered or exposed text node in the body, holding at least one letter, has no lang or xml:lang on itself or any ancestor. Nodes of only digits, punctuation or icon-font glyphs do not count, since they may not be read as text elements. That text is a text element, or part of one, under any reading of the wording, so the second route fails for it; the first fails because html has no attribute; the fault proves the test fails. Everything else is cannot_tell, by stated rules: an empty attribute or one that does not fit the document type (the wording says the indication is given, and does not say whether an empty or unsuitable attribute gives it), and a page without an html attribute where every rendered text node is covered, which may meet the second route but cannot be shown to. The link examines both routes, decided or abstained on, for the whole page, so it is resolving and its fault means failure. The entry is full: the tool may say passed only through the html element, failed only on uncovered rendered text, and needs review otherwise. A page that meets the test only through the second route is outside what the check supports and gets needs review. axe's html-has-lang is evidence only: it looks only at the html element, so a page that uses the second route gets a fault although it meets the test. axe's html-xml-lang-mismatch is tagged but not linked: it compares the base language of lang and xml:lang when both are on the html element, which says nothing about whether either route is met. Applicability is always: the test applies to every page, and the check never answers inapplicable. Needs is empty: attributes are read on the page as loaded.

citations.quote: est donnée sur chaque élément de texte ou sur l’un des éléments parents
Dans chaque page web, la langue par défaut est-elle présente
Si c’est le cas, **le test est validé**.
Pour XHTML 1.0 servi en "text/html" : attribut lang et xml:lang obligatoires ;
